findings.claim: get_pager_file wraps the pager stream buffer in MaybeStripAnsi and flushes the wrapper in a finally block, which can interact badly with Click's testing streams that are closed on exit
findings.explanation: echo_via_pager delegates to get_pager_file. In 8.4 get_pager_file creates a MaybeStripAnsi wrapper around stream.buffer and yields it, then flushes the wrapper in finally. Flushing/closing the TextIOWrapper can close the underlying borrowed buffer, so when CliRunner later flushes sys.stdout the underlying file is already closed, producing ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.

citations.quote:
with _pager_contextmanager(color=color) as (stream, encoding, color):
        # Split streams by capabilities rather than the abstract TextIO /
        # BinaryIO annotations: buffered text streams can be unwrapped to bytes,
        # while text-only streams are yielded as-is.
        if _has_binary_buffer(stream):
            # Text stream backed by a binary buffer.
            stream = MaybeStripAnsi(stream.buffer, color=color, encoding=encoding)
        elif isinstance(stream, t.BinaryIO):
            # Binary stream
            stream = MaybeStripAnsi(stream, color=color, encoding=encoding)
        try:
            yield stream
        finally:
            stream.flush()
